highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. highlights.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # Edge AI inference offers telecoms a new growth engine Edge AI inference could become a new growth engine for the telecommunications industry, potentially placing telcos closer to the center of AI infrastructure. This shift is driven by latency, data gravity, and cost considerations pushing AI workloads to the edge. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Oct 30, 2026 at 05:30 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Edge AI inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for telecom operators. * Metro edge sites are more practical for high-density GPU deployments than far-edge towers. * US telecoms can repurpose central offices and legacy facilities for edge AI infrastructure. * Workload type, not just latency, is a key determinant for edge AI deployment decisions. [Edge AI](/tag/edge+ai) inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for the telecommunications industry, potentially positioning telcos closer to the core of [AI inference](/tag/ai+inference) infrastructure. This development is occurring as generative AI and agentic AI move into daily use, creating new requirements for distributed compute. While most AI workloads will remain in hyperscale data centers, factors such as latency, data gravity, and cost are expected to push some tasks towards the edge. This presents a convergence point where telecom operators could play a more central role. ### The Nuances of Edge AI Deployment [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) has already indicated this opportunity, with projects and partnerships involving companies like AT&T, Charter Communications, Cisco, Nokia, SoftBank, Telefónica, and T-Mobile. Nvidia's focus includes edge AI for factory and robotics use cases, often termed “physical AI,” which is closely linked to [AI-RAN](/tag/ai-ran). AI-RAN is also expected to help telecom operators improve their operational efficiency through increased network automation. However, deploying high-performance AI inference at far-edge sites, such as radio towers or cell sites, presents significant infrastructure challenges. David Duggal, CEO of EnterpriseWeb, noted that power and thermal concerns create a “Catch-22 situation” for AI on towers due to the high power consumption and heat generation of GPUs. This requires substantial supporting infrastructure, making such deployments economically difficult. The Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) is working to define unified practices for AI data center infrastructure. Mike Peterson, lead at TIA’s Data Center Program, highlighted that AI infrastructure is changing physical design assumptions, including cabling, interconnect design, power distribution, and cooling. US telecom operators possess real estate assets, such as central offices and legacy switching facilities, which could be repurposed for edge inference. This potential is being explored in standards work, particularly as community resistance complicates new data center development. ### Latency vs. Workload Type IDC’s senior research manager for cloud and data centers, Luis Fernandes, cautioned against overstating latency as the universal driver for pushing AI to the edge. Research by IDC and the European Commission found that while latency matters in specific cases, workload type is often a more determining factor. Real-time workloads necessitate instant responses shaped by local context, while analytical workloads typically do not. Startups including Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo are quietly routing calls and real-world tasks to human workers when their software can't handle the job, according to a [CNBC investigation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The revelation exposes a gap between the industry's automation promises and the messy reality of deploying AI agents that actually work. As companies race to launch AI agent products, the human fallback strategy raises questions about whether the technology is ready for prime time or if we're witnessing another round of AI overpromising. The AI agent boom is running into a very human problem. While startups pitch their products as autonomous software that can handle everything from customer service to appointment scheduling, the reality behind the curtain looks a lot more manual than advertised. Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo - three startups building AI agent platforms - are all using human workers to complete tasks when their AI systems fall short, according to [CNBC's reporting](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The companies route phone calls, handle complex customer requests, and manage other real-world interactions to human operators when their algorithms can't figure out what to do. It's a pragmatic solution to a thorny problem. AI agents work great in demos and controlled environments, but real-world deployment is messier. Customers ask unexpected questions, systems integrate poorly, and edge cases pop up constantly. Rather than let their products fail visibly, these startups built human safety nets. Advertisement The approach isn't new. The AI industry has a long history of "pseudo-AI" - products that appear automated but rely heavily on human labor. Amazon's Just Walk Out technology, which seemed to let shoppers grab items and leave without checkout, reportedly used [over 1,000 workers in India](https://www.theverge.com/2024/4/5/24122070/amazon-just-walk-out-grocery-stores-humans) reviewing transactions. Facebook's AI content moderation has always depended on thousands of human moderators doing the actual work. What makes the current wave different is the stakes. Companies are deploying AI agents to handle sensitive tasks like healthcare scheduling, financial transactions, and customer support. When the AI fails and a human has to step in, there's often no transparency about who's actually handling your data or request. Customers ask unexpected questions, systems integrate poorly, and edge cases pop up constantly. Rather than let their products fail visibly, these startups built human safety nets. Amazon's Just Walk Out technology, which seemed to let shoppers grab items and leave without checkout, reportedly used [over 1,000 workers in India](https://www.theverge.com/2024/4/5/24122070/amazon-just-walk-out-grocery-stores-humans) reviewing transactions. Facebook's AI content moderation has always depended on thousands of human moderators doing the actual work. What makes the current wave different is the stakes. For three decades, the internet was built around one central assumption: humans would use it. People searched for information, read articles, watched videos, compared products, clicked advertisements and visited websites. Much of the digital economy was therefore designed around human attention. That assumption is now being challenged by the rapid emergence of AI agents. AI agents do more than answer questions. They can search, browse websites, compare information, fill forms, manage tasks and increasingly make transactions on behalf of users. In September, OpenAI introduced new autonomous agent capabilities designed to pursue goals across applications, while other companies are developing systems that can plan trips, shop for groceries and manage subscriptions. ## **From Search Engines to Machine Users** Traditional search engines sent people from one website to another. Users opened links, read different sources and decided what to believe or buy. AI systems are changing that process by bringing information together inside the interface itself. The user may receive a synthesized answer without visiting most of the websites from which the information came. The next stage is more significant. AI agents can interact directly with websites and perform actions rather than merely retrieve information. Cloudflare now describes these systems as a second audience for the internet and says that AI-agent requests on its network increased by more than 1,700% over the past year. highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Startups including Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo are quietly routing calls and real-world tasks to human workers when their software can't handle the job, according to a [CNBC investigation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The revelation exposes a gap between the industry's automation promises and the messy reality of deploying AI agents that actually work. As companies race to launch AI agent products, the human fallback strategy raises questions about whether the technology is ready for prime time or if we're witnessing another round of AI overpromising. The AI agent boom is running into a very human problem. While startups pitch their products as autonomous software that can handle everything from customer service to appointment scheduling, the reality behind the curtain looks a lot more manual than advertised. Dazzle, Duckbill, and Wajo - three startups building AI agent platforms - are all using human workers to complete tasks when their AI systems fall short, according to [CNBC's reporting](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/ai-agents-humans-dazzle-duckbill-meta.html). The companies route phone calls, handle complex customer requests, and manage other real-world interactions to human operators when their algorithms can't figure out what to do. It's a pragmatic solution to a thorny problem. AI agents work great in demos and controlled environments, but real-world deployment is messier. Customers ask unexpected questions, systems integrate poorly, and edge cases pop up constantly. Rather than let their products fail visibly, these startups built human safety nets. Advertisement The approach isn't new. The AI industry has a long history of "pseudo-AI" - products that appear automated but rely heavily on human labor. Amazon's Just Walk Out technology, which seemed to let shoppers grab items and leave without checkout, reportedly used [over 1,000 workers in India](https://www.theverge.com/2024/4/5/24122070/amazon-just-walk-out-grocery-stores-humans) reviewing transactions. Facebook's AI content moderation has always depended on thousands of human moderators doing the actual work. What makes the current wave different is the stakes. Companies are deploying AI agents to handle sensitive tasks like healthcare scheduling, financial transactions, and customer support. For three decades, the internet was built around one central assumption: humans would use it. People searched for information, read articles, watched videos, compared products, clicked advertisements and visited websites. Much of the digital economy was therefore designed around human attention. That assumption is now being challenged by the rapid emergence of AI agents. AI agents do more than answer questions. They can search, browse websites, compare information, fill forms, manage tasks and increasingly make transactions on behalf of users. In September, OpenAI introduced new autonomous agent capabilities designed to pursue goals across applications, while other companies are developing systems that can plan trips, shop for groceries and manage subscriptions. ## **From Search Engines to Machine Users** Traditional search engines sent people from one website to another. Users opened links, read different sources and decided what to believe or buy. AI systems are changing that process by bringing information together inside the interface itself. The user may receive a synthesized answer without visiting most of the websites from which the information came. The next stage is more significant. AI agents can interact directly with websites and perform actions rather than merely retrieve information. Cloudflare now describes these systems as a second audience for the internet and says that AI-agent requests on its network increased by more than 1,700% over the past year. It also reported that more than half of internet traffic on its network is now non-human. This does not mean that humans have disappeared from the internet. It means that the web now has another rapidly expanding audience. That audience does not browse in the same way as people do. It does not care about page design, advertisements or scrolling. It is software acting on behalf of people. ## **The Crisis for the Open Web** This development creates a serious economic problem for publishers. LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Two caveats on the rest of the family. Alibaba announced updates to Qwen3.8-Max at its Apsara Conference on October 28, 2026, including 33 automated improvement cycles and a rise in its Artificial Analysis score from 40 to 45, according to [Philstar’s report on the conference](https://www.philstar.com/business/technology/2026/10/28/2566097/alibaba-unveils-roadmap-full-stack-ai-strategy-chips-cloud-infrastructure-models-agents). The feature will be available for testing in the latest iOS developer beta starting Nov. 4 and will launch with the official iOS 27.3 release in December, Alibaba said. Qwen’s AI capabilities will be integrated into several Apple features, including Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence. Users can choose whether to enable the integration and what information to share. Alibaba said user requests and generated responses would not be used to train its AI models. The feature will be available on compatible iPhones whose device location and Apple Account region are both set to China. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the partnership would bring new AI-powered services to Chinese users. Wang Xiaojie, an AI expert at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, said this marked the first time a major global consumer hardware maker had adopted a Chinese large language model as LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Omnii-1 Phages Reach 1 Patient, Outcome Unshared [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 16 min read A company called Radical Numerics says it has given a human patient a cocktail of AI-designed viruses to fight an antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection. [TechRadar framed the story](https://www.techradar.com/pro/a-human-subject-has-been-injected-with-an-ai-designed-virus-aiming-to-kill-antibiotic-resistant-bacteria-so-lets-see-how-that-turns-out) with a pointed headline: let’s see how that turns out. That caution fits the facts. The company announced the treatment on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and as of October 31 it had not said whether the patient improved. The viruses in question are bacteriophages, usually shortened to phages. They infect bacteria and leave human cells alone. Radical Numerics says its biological AI model, Omnii-1, generated the phage designs used in the cocktail. The firm calls this the first clinical use of AI-designed phages, a claim that rests entirely on the company’s own announcement for now. This article separates what is documented from what is missing. It also looks at why a purpose-built biology model matters for the wider AI market, where narrow specialist systems keep challenging general-purpose giants, as in the [Samaya Sterling finance-agent results](https://shattered.io/samaya-sterling-3b-active-finance-agent-frontierfinance-58-9-percent-2026/) we covered earlier this month. The gap between a lab result and a cured patient is wide, and the announcement sits on the near side of it. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## What Radical Numerics Actually Announced The announcement came on October 20, 2026. Radical Numerics said designs generated by Omnii-1 were administered to a patient with an antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection. It described the route as an authorised, physician-led compassionate-use pathway. In the company’s own words, this was “the world’s first clinical use of AI-designed phages.” The second claim concerns the laboratory. According to the company, the cocktail eliminated the patient’s resistant bacterial isolate in a dish before anything reached the patient. [The Register reported the statement](https://www.theregister.com/science/2026/10/22/human-receives-ai-designed-virus-for-the-first-time/5304874) in its coverage two days later. Radical Numerics put it this way: “The cocktail containing Omnii-1-designed phage variants eliminated the patient’s antibiotic-resistant isolate in vitro.” Read that sentence slowly. The word “in vitro” means the kill happened outside the body, in a controlled lab setting. It says nothing about what the cocktail did once inside a person. The company has not claimed otherwise, and it has not stated whether the treatment helped the patient or cleared the infection. Per the announcement, Omnii-1 is a biological AI model that covers DNA, RNA and proteins, among other uses. The phage work is one application, and the company picked it as its public proof point. For a young AI-biology firm, a human case is a strong marketing asset, which is one reason readers should weigh the claim against the evidence offered rather than the headline. ## What Is Still Not Disclosed About the Patient The list of missing details is longer than the list of confirmed ones. Radical Numerics has not named the patient, the diagnosis, the treating physicians, the dose, or the clinical outcome. LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Neuron-Derived AI Video Model Debuts at 5x Speed [2026] ![Dr. Elena Marchetti](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/emarchetti.webp) [Dr. Elena Marchetti](https://shattered.io/author/emarchetti/) Updated Nov 1, 2026 · 15 min read The Biological Computing Co., a San Francisco startup better known as TBC, released an image-to-video model called **TBC mischief 1** on October 30, 2026. According to the company’s PR Newswire announcement, it is the world’s first publicly available **neuron-derived AI video model**. The pitch is simple: living neurons grown in a lab taught TBC’s researchers some efficiency tricks, and those tricks now run as a thin software layer on top of an existing open-weight video model. The headline numbers are aggressive. TBC says mischief 1 generates video about five times faster than its base model, Wan 2.2, at comparable quality, with pricing that starts at half a cent per second of output. If those claims hold up under independent testing, they would put real pressure on a crowded field. Our [ranking of AI video generators](https://shattered.io/best-ai-video-generators-kling-4-veo-3-1-sora-shutdown-2026/) shows how fast that field has been moving, and cost per clip is now one of the few levers left that buyers can compare directly. This analysis walks through what TBC actually announced, what the neurons did and did not do, the pricing math for production teams, and where the evidence stops. TNW (The Next Web) pointed out that the company has not published independent tests backing the speed claim, and that gap shapes almost everything below. We also include a claims-versus-evidence table, a competitive read, and five predictions. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## What TBC Mischief 1 Is and What Shipped on October 30 Mischief 1 is an image-to-video model. A user supplies a starting image and a text prompt, and the model returns a short clip. Per the TBC release, it is built on Wan 2.2, an open-weight video model that TNW describes as Alibaba’s. TBC does not claim to have trained a new foundation model from scratch. It claims to have added an optimization layer that makes the existing one faster and cheaper to run. The model went live on two AI marketplaces, fal and OpenRouter. TBC says it is the lowest-priced image-to-video model on both. Reporting from Tao Media adds that an AWS Marketplace listing is marked as coming soon, which fits with the AWS partnership TBC announced on September 22, 2026. Tao Media also lists the output specs. Clips run 3 or 5 seconds, at 480p or 720p in landscape, at 16 frames per second, delivered as MP4. Those are modest numbers next to the cinematic-length, high-resolution clips that top-tier closed models advertise. The product is aimed at volume and price, not at maximum visual ambition. The company’s leadership is small and named. Alex Ksendzovsky is co-founder and CEO, and Jon Pomeraniec is co-founder and COO. LLMs.content: ![Zee Business](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/images/2025/zeebiz_logo_new.svg) ![Live TV](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/zeebiz_revamp/images/tv.svg) ![Live TV](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/zeebiz_revamp/images/tv.svg) ![comscore](https://sb.scorecardresearch.com/p?c1=2&c2=9254297&cv=2.0&cj=1) ![](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/zeebiz_revamp/images/icons/link.svg) ![](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/zeebiz_revamp/images/icons/share.svg) # Canva launches Brush AI model to edit designs with prompts, cuts editing costs by 46% ![Canva launches Brush AI model to edit designs with prompts, cuts editing costs by 46% ](https://cdn.zeebiz.com/sites/default/files/2026/10/31/416975-untitled-design-2026-10-31t141324858.jpg?im=FitAndFill=(848,477)&format=webp&quality=medium) To create an easier editing process for existing designs, Canva has launched a new vision-language model, Canva Brush, that lets users use natural language prompts. The new AI model is built to grasp and recalibrate specific parts of a design while retaining the rest of the layout, typography, colours and imagery. Canva Brush is part of Canva's focus on enhancing its artificial intelligence-based design features. The model is different from image generation tools which are used to make images from the ground up. The model is a process for editing and refining existing images as opposed to creating images from scratch. It can reportedly accommodate changes, whether that is a single line of text, or changes to several slides in a presentation. Canva claims that the model is 46 per cent more economical per edit task and up to 69 per cent faster at performing general design editing tasks compared to the previous design agent. The feature is initially available for supported design edits to Canva Pro subscribers. ## **What is Canva Brush AI Model?** Canva Brush is a vision-language model developed by Canva's in-house Canva Research team. It incorporates aspects of visual comprehension and the interpretation of written instructions, enabling the user to manipulate the design using common language. The model can review an existing design, comprehend its components and apply changes requested without making unnecessary alterations to other components of the design. For example, a user might ask it to change a heading, modify the colour scheme, add imagery to a presentation or restyle a presentation. It also comes with the ability to ensure consistency throughout several pages, such as typography, spacing, colours and layouts. ## **How to Use Canva Brush?** Canva Brush allows for an agentic process of making and revising changes to designs. It can write and execute code to tweak individual design components, review the modified page and then, based on that review, modify the page again. For instance, a user can instruct it to develop a three-page pitch deck for a bakery that has Art Nouveau backgrounds and graphics. The model can arrange content across the pages, create, position and choose appropriate imagery, and create a consistent visual style. According to Canva, everything that you create or edit with the Brush is still editable. After the AI has finished, users can tweak the text, images, colours, layout, etc. to suit the design. ## **Canva Brush performance: 69% quicker editing, 46% less expensive** According to Canva, Brush is up to 69 per cent quicker for basic design editing tasks, and also has a 46 per cent lower cost per edit task, compared with its previous design agent. The company claimed that it tested its model against its own previous system, and found it to be anywhere from equal to the best to best in terms of quality on most edit jobs. It was said to give exceptional results when transforming and adapting old designs to new formats. Open Source AI.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Run an LLM Locally: Qwen3.8-27B in 12 Steps, 75 Min [2026] ![Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Oct 31, 2026 · 33 min read Qwen3.8-27B is the member of the Qwen3.8 family that a single workstation can actually host. The Qwen model listing shows the dense 27-billion-parameter model, along with a matching FP8 release, dating to August 13, 2026, and [the Qwen Cloud page for Qwen3.8-27B](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-27b) now sits next to community GGUF builds that run in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio. If you want to run an LLM locally in late October 2026, this is the model to size your machine against. Running it takes three pieces. You need weights that fit in memory, a server that speaks the OpenAI wire format, and a way to measure whether the result is fast enough to use. Most guides stop after the second piece and leave you guessing about the third. The steps below build all three in roughly 75 minutes, and most of that is download time. For a chat front end on top of the same server, our [llama.cpp and Open WebUI walkthrough](https://shattered.io/llama-cpp-server-open-webui-gguf-12-steps-2026/) picks up where Step 6 ends. Local inference is no longer a hobby corner. In the 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey, 14.4% of professional developers who use AI tools selected Ollama, and [the survey’s technology section](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology) shows large language models among the tools more than a quarter of all respondents use or want to use. Numbers like that explain why people search for ways to run an LLM locally, and why a repeatable benchmark matters more than a screenshot of one lucky run. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. [Add now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Fshattered.io%2F) ## Why Qwen3.8-27B Is the Local Model to Start With Alibaba’s Qwen line moved to the Qwen3.8 generation over the summer. The family now spans a very large open flagship, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, which carries 2.4 trillion total parameters with about 95 billion active per token, and a set of smaller releases meant for ordinary hardware. The 27B model is the one sized for a desktop. It is a dense causal language model with a vision encoder, so it reads images and video as well as text, and it offers an adjustable reasoning mode that you can switch on for hard problems and off for quick answers. Dense matters for local use. A mixture-of-experts model activates only a slice of its weights per token, which helps speed, but you still need memory for all the experts. A dense 27B model has no such trick. Every weight is read for every generated token, so memory bandwidth sets your speed ceiling and file size sets your memory floor. That makes the arithmetic in this guide simple and predictable, which is exactly what you want when you are sizing a machine. The official model repository documents Transformers, vLLM and SGLang as supported runtimes. llama.cpp support arrives through GGUF files that community members convert and upload. That split shapes the whole tutorial. The weights come from Qwen, the quantized files usually come from third parties, and you need a habit of checking one against the other. Step 5 covers how. Open Source AI.content: # [AI Changes Everything](/) # AI Week in Review 26.10.31 ### Gemini 4 Carbon, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, GPT-6.1 Terra, Mistral Large 4 weights out, Genie 4, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, LFM3, Lumma-Fev-v2, GitHub Copilot Fusion, AI disproves ETH! Google reported cybersecurity scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71% on CWE-bench for patching. Released just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon’s general release, this release of Gemini 4 Carbon puts Google firmly back at the frontier of AI, with a speed of iteration that should keep it there. The help assess frontier AI models better, **[Artificial Analysis has updated their Intelligence Index to v5](https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/artificial-analysis-intelligence-index-v5)** and has a new separate Progress Index for tracking model capabilities over time. Intelligence Index v5 is based on updated set of 9 evaluation benchmarks, adding FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench-Science to the AAII v5. It assigns equal weight to knowledge work, coding, science, and general intelligence, with 60% of its score based on private test sets or withheld answers. This new AAII v5 shakes up AI model rankings. GPT-6 Astra at 57 is well above Claude Fable 5.1 at 49, and Chinese open weights AI models fall further behind: Kimi K3.1 Pro is at 46, while other the top Chinese open weights models are barely above Gemini 3.8 Flash (31) in rankings. Figure 2. The new AAII v5 uses more rigorous benchmarks with private test sets, improving index quality and shaking up some rankings. Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon leads the v5 ranking. The Progress Index places models released since 2022 on a continuous capability scale to support comparisons across different generations. As AI has improved since 2022, individual benchmarks became saturated and were replaced; the Progress Index digests those shifts and helps normalize AI model capability assessment over time. Figure 3. The Progress Index for AI models since November 2022 shows that AI models have progressed enormously, continuing up and to the right on the Progress Index. #### New AI product and AI model releases **[OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-1-terra/)**, a fast and efficient model that excels at visual reasoning and computer use, scoring 51 on AAII v5. Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # Edge AI inference offers telecoms a new growth engine Edge AI inference could become a new growth engine for the telecommunications industry, potentially placing telcos closer to the center of AI infrastructure. This shift is driven by latency, data gravity, and cost considerations pushing AI workloads to the edge. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Oct 30, 2026 at 05:30 PM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Edge AI inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for telecom operators. * Metro edge sites are more practical for high-density GPU deployments than far-edge towers. * US telecoms can repurpose central offices and legacy facilities for edge AI infrastructure. * Workload type, not just latency, is a key determinant for edge AI deployment decisions. [Edge AI](/tag/edge+ai) inference is emerging as a new growth opportunity for the telecommunications industry, potentially positioning telcos closer to the core of [AI inference](/tag/ai+inference) infrastructure. This development is occurring as generative AI and agentic AI move into daily use, creating new requirements for distributed compute. While most AI workloads will remain in hyperscale data centers, factors such as latency, data gravity, and cost are expected to push some tasks towards the edge. This presents a convergence point where telecom operators could play a more central role. ### The Nuances of Edge AI Deployment [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) has already indicated this opportunity, with projects and partnerships involving companies like AT&T, Charter Communications, Cisco, Nokia, SoftBank, Telefónica, and T-Mobile. Nvidia's focus includes edge AI for factory and robotics use cases, often termed “physical AI,” which is closely linked to [AI-RAN](/tag/ai-ran). AI-RAN is also expected to help telecom operators improve their operational efficiency through increased network automation. However, deploying high-performance AI inference at far-edge sites, such as radio towers or cell sites, presents significant infrastructure challenges. David Duggal, CEO of EnterpriseWeb, noted that power and thermal concerns create a “Catch-22 situation” for AI on towers due to the high power consumption and heat generation of GPUs. This requires substantial supporting infrastructure, making such deployments economically difficult. The Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA) is working to define unified practices for AI data center infrastructure. Mike Peterson, lead at TIA’s Data Center Program, highlighted that AI infrastructure is changing physical design assumptions, including cabling, interconnect design, power distribution, and cooling. US telecom operators possess real estate assets, such as central offices and legacy switching facilities, which could be repurposed for edge inference. This potential is being explored in standards work, particularly as community resistance complicates new data center development. ### Latency vs. Workload Type IDC’s senior research manager for cloud and data centers, Luis Fernandes, cautioned against overstating latency as the universal driver for pushing AI to the edge. Research by IDC and the European Commission found that while latency matters in specific cases, workload type is often a more determining factor. Real-time workloads necessitate instant responses shaped by local context, while analytical workloads typically do not. Infra & Chips.content: × Search Pulse 2.0 # General Compute Raises $100 Million Series A To Build Inference Cloud For Alternative AI Chips By Amit Chowdhry [![Pulse 2.0](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/logo-white.png)](https://pulse2.com "Pulse 2.0") General Compute Raises $100 Million Series A To Build Inference Cloud For Alternative AI Chips [![Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn](https://pulse2.com/wp-content/themes/pulse2/images/inp2.png)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pulse2news) General Compute has raised $100 million in Series A funding co-led by Blackbird and Abstract to build a heterogeneous AI inference cloud using specialized chips from Cerebras, SambaNova, Positron AI, and other hardware providers. Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global, Bold Capital, QED Investors, 645 Ventures, Carbide Ventures, Uncorrelated Fund, Endeavor Catalyst, Icehouse Ventures, MatterScale, Carya, Plug and Play, and other investors also participated in the round. General Compute is building infrastructure designed specifically for AI inference as demand for faster token generation grows. The company gives customers access to both GPUs and specialized inference chips through a single cloud platform and flexible commercial agreement. Its first major deployments are expected to go live in the first quarter of 2027, and General Compute said it has more than 50 MW of capacity in its development pipeline. The company’s platform is designed to handle the operational complexity associated with deploying different types of AI hardware. General Compute purchases the equipment, installs it in colocation facilities, and manages networking, power, cooling, software, and operations. Customers can then route workloads to the hardware architecture best suited for a particular task without procuring or operating the infrastructure themselves. General Compute supports systems from Cerebras, SambaNova, and Positron AI and is designed to run models from major AI laboratories as well as open-source models. Its intelligent workload-routing technology dynamically selects hardware based on the requirements of individual agentic calls and other inference workloads. Customers can purchase compute through guaranteed tokens-per-second service-level agreements or dedicated bare-metal infrastructure. General Compute has also secured a debt facility of up to $400 million from Upper90 to finance the expansion of its neocloud infrastructure. The company sees inference as an increasingly important part of AI infrastructure spending as laboratories shift more computing resources from training models to serving them in production. General Compute is positioning itself around specialized silicon rather than relying exclusively on GPUs, arguing that different architectures can provide better economics and performance for particular inference workloads. The company was founded by CEO Finn Puklowski and CTO Jason Goodison and is headquartered in San Francisco. The new equity financing, combined with the Upper90 debt facility and General Compute’s hardware partnerships, will support deployment of additional inference capacity as the company works to establish a cloud platform spanning multiple generations and types of AI accelerators. **KEY QUOTES:** *“The era of one-size-fits-all AI hardware is over. Infra & Chips.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Holdings](/stocklist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast)[Influencer Tracker](/influencer) # South Korea Exports Nearly Double, Fastest Growth Since 1974 on AI Chip Demand [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) South Korea's exports rose 93.7% year on year in October to $115.28 billion, the fastest growth since January 1974 and slightly above economists' forecasts. Semiconductor shipments jumped 259.4% and computer exports surged 496.6% as global technology companies kept investing in AI infrastructure. The trade ministry also cited more working days because of the timing of the Chuseok holiday. Imports climbed 36.0% to $72.78 billion, the biggest annual increase since January 2022, leaving a trade surplus of $42.50 billion, down from September's record $49.97 billion. ##### Key Elements ![South Korea Exports Nearly Double, Fastest Growth Since 1974 on AI Chip Demand](https://img.biggo.com/JXXgDV-ctv-YdxDFRqzY0HFM26tKxq6XcFJYHw_79oc/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzY1OTI2MTJmLTBlZDktNDAwNS1hY2M0LWE2MjkzZWEwODcyMV8xNzkzNDk4OTE3X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) South Korea's exports almost doubled in October from a year earlier, the sharpest annual increase in more than half a century, as demand tied to artificial intelligence lifted semiconductor and computer shipments. Overseas sales rose 93.7% to $115.28 billion last month, the trade ministry said Sunday, slightly above the 93.2% median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists. The gain topped September's 83.7% advance and was the fastest since January 1974. The ministry pointed to a calendar quirk as well: the timing of the Chuseok holiday left more working days in October than a year earlier, inflating the year-on-year comparison. Chip exports jumped 259.4%, with prices and volumes holding high as major global technology companies keep spending on facilities in the race for AI leadership. Computer shipments climbed even faster, up 496.6%, driven by server demand for AI services. | Indicator | October | Year-on-year change | | --- | --- | --- | | Exports | $115.28 billion | +93.7% | | Imports | $72.78 billion | +36.0% | | Trade balance | $42.50 billion surplus | - | | Semiconductor exports | - | +259.4% | | Computer exports | - | +496.6% | Note: Trade balance compares with a record $49.97 billion surplus in September. Imports rose 36.0% to $72.78 billion, accelerating from a 26.0% increase in September and marking the largest annual gain since January 2022. The monthly trade surplus came in at $42.50 billion, narrower than September's record $49.97 billion, as import growth picked up while export revenue stayed far above the import bill. South Korea, Asia's fourth-largest economy, is closely watched as a gauge of global trade because of its role in electronics and manufactured goods. October's figures underline how much of that trade momentum now rests on AI-related spending, with chipmakers benefiting from expanding data center investment. For investors, the data reinforce the case that AI infrastructure demand remains a powerful driver of Korean export earnings, though the calendar effect means part of October's headline rate reflects the comparison base rather than underlying volume alone. Infra & Chips.content: Sunday, November 1, 2026 [![newlogo ER](https://www.eurasiareview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/cropped-newlogo-1.jpeg)](https://www.eurasiareview.com/) ### [Eurasia Review](https://www.eurasiareview.com/ "Eurasia Review") A Journal of Analysis and News ![The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production - OpEd](https://www.eurasiareview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/a-1-800x445.jpg) [Opinion](https://www.eurasiareview.com/category/opinion/) [1](https://www.eurasiareview.com/category/1/) [Technology](https://www.eurasiareview.com/category/technology/) # The Global AI Chip Race Needs Proof, Not Just Production – OpEd [Burak Oktenli](https://www.eurasiareview.com/author/burak-oktenli/ "Burak Oktenli") [0 Comments](https://www.eurasiareview.com/01112026-the-global-ai-chip-race-needs-proof-not-just-production-oped/#respond) By [Burak Oktenli](https://www.eurasiareview.com/author/burak-oktenli/ "Posts by Burak Oktenli") ## **Key Takeaways:** * On 23 October OpenAI reported that AI agents in separate virtual machines exchanged synthetic secrets via processor-cache timing without a network connection, showing that software isolation does not fully prevent covert channels through shared hardware. * Distinct hardware risks such as Rowhammer-style DRAM bit flips (demonstrated on tested SK Hynix DDR5 modules) and firmware flaws require specific, independently verified tests; manufacturing location or capacity alone does not guarantee security boundaries. * Procurement for critical systems should demand documented evidence of tested isolation claims, failure behavior and recovery paths rather than relying on origin labels or general assurances, matching requirements to risk while supporting shared validation capacity. *OpenAI’s latest security tests show how isolated AI workloads can communicate through shared hardware. Governments racing to build chip capacity must also demand evidence of isolation, memory integrity, and recovery.* On October 23, OpenAI reported a result that should interest every government investing in advanced AI infrastructure. In a controlled experiment, agents running in separate virtual machines exchanged synthetic secrets without an ordinary network connection or shared writable files. They used timing differences in the processor cache, a physical resource both environments could affect. [The company disclosed the test and the monitoring changes it made](https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/). This was not evidence that AI had physically damaged a chip, stolen real customer information, or defeated every form of isolation. In most communication tests, the researchers steered agents toward particular channels or supplied protocols. The narrower result is still consequential: software separation does not automatically eliminate communication through shared machinery. Two days earlier, [AI-assisted discovery of serious PHP software vulnerabilities](https://apnews.com/article/a0af9576808a0963efca8df14d4b5183) prompted an international patching scramble affecting government and other websites. These were software flaws, not hardware attacks. Together, the episodes illustrate how quickly security research can expose unexpected weaknesses while the organizations running essential services struggle to respond. The policy lesson arrives as governments compete to expand semiconductor production. The [European Commission’s proposed Chips Act 2.0](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/proposal-chips-act-20) seeks capacity and supply-chain resilience, while the United States and Asian producers remain central to advanced chips and memory. Manufacturing location matters for availability and geopolitical leverage. Governments racing to build chip capacity must also demand evidence of isolation, memory integrity, and recovery.* On October 23, OpenAI reported a result that should interest every government investing in advanced AI infrastructure. In a controlled experiment, agents running in separate virtual machines exchanged synthetic secrets without an ordinary network connection or shared writable files. They used timing differences in the processor cache, a physical resource both environments could affect. [The company disclosed the test and the monitoring changes it made](https://openai.com/index/securing-our-frontier-model-training-environment/). This was not evidence that AI had physically damaged a chip, stolen real customer information, or defeated every form of isolation. In most communication tests, the researchers steered agents toward particular channels or supplied protocols. The narrower result is still consequential: software separation does not automatically eliminate communication through shared machinery. Two days earlier, [AI-assisted discovery of serious PHP software vulnerabilities](https://apnews.com/article/a0af9576808a0963efca8df14d4b5183) prompted an international patching scramble affecting government and other websites. These were software flaws, not hardware attacks. Together, the episodes illustrate how quickly security research can expose unexpected weaknesses while the organizations running essential services struggle to respond. The policy lesson arrives as governments compete to expand semiconductor production. The [European Commission’s proposed Chips Act 2.0](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/proposal-chips-act-20) seeks capacity and supply-chain resilience, while the United States and Asian producers remain central to advanced chips and memory. Manufacturing location matters for availability and geopolitical leverage.
